sentences.text: It is, inter alia, contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is innocent lady, having no concern what-so-ever with the allegations levelled by the complainant.
He further contends that even from the perusal of the FIR (Annexure P-1), the allegations levelled are against the husband of the petitioner.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner referred to the legal notice dated 06.10.2023 (Annexure P-2) given by learned counsel for the complainant to the husband of the petitioner only and it is specifically mentioned in the said notice that 21 cheques had been given by the husband of the petitioner.
He further contends that there is no overtact attributed to the petitioner nor any money was ever given to her and the petitioner is ready to join investigation.

4. Notice of motion.
5.
On the asking of the Court, Mr. Subhash Godara, Addl. AG, Punjab, present in Court, accepts notice on behalf of the State-respondent and prays for time to file the status report/reply in the matter.

6. Adjourned to 16.11.2023.
7.

Needful be done well before the date fixed with an advance copy to the counsel opposite.
8.

In the meanwhile, the petitioner is hereby directed to join investigation within seven days from today and in the event of her arrest, she is ordered to be released on interim bail on her furnishing personal/surety bonds to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer/Investigating Officer.
She shall also abide by conditions as envisaged under Section 438(2) Cr.P.C."

5. Keeping in view the above submissions made by learned State counsel and the fact that the petitioner had joined the investigation consequent to the order dated 20.10.2023 passed by this Court, interim bail granted vide order dated 20.10.2023 is hereby confirmed, subject to conditions as envisaged under Section 438(2) Cr.P.C.

Further the petitioner is directed to join investigation as and when required in future by way of written notice for such purpose to be served by Investigating Officer of this case upon the petitioner; he will not tamper with the evidence nor will influence the witnesses and will not leave the country without prior permission of the Court.
(SANJIV BERRY)
